public_rationale: Contemporaneous reporting explains the $7 billion figure as expected spending. A later Epoch reconstruction reaches roughly that scale when broader research compute is included, but explicitly retains projections and an amortization assumption. This makes the figure plausible as a broad estimate without establishing the completed-year training-and-inference cost asserted in the post. The records also do not establish a sufficiently comparable contrary total.
limitations: Primary financial records isolating the relevant expenses were not obtained.
The original report was inaccessible; its forecasts are represented through a readable secondary summary.
A broader reading that includes all research compute has more support, but changes the metric's scope.

our_interpretation: The ordinary reading is expenditure attributable to calendar 2024, not a forecast made during that year.
The post cites press estimates, so the accounting basis is estimate.
Around $7 billion allows ordinary approximation, but does not license substituting all research spending or annualized commitments for training and inference expenditure.
Training may include preparatory runs and related model work; the source does not precisely delimit those costs.
criteria.support_condition: Reliable retrospective estimates or records place combined calendar-2024 training and inference expenditure near $7 billion on a consistent scope.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Reliable retrospective evidence places that same expenditure materially away from $7 billion, with uncertainty small enough to exclude ordinary approximation.

evidence.explanation: The article reports expected training spending and separately forecasts approximately $4 billion of inference spending. These explain the roughly $7 billion figure's origin, but are not completed-year results.

Epoch reconstructs roughly $7 billion of research, training and inference compute, but its inputs include final-quarter projections and an assumed research amortization schedule. It therefore offers approximate corroboration under a broader scope, not a settled realized training-and-inference total.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: A retrospective 2024 expense breakdown separating training, inference and other research, with consistent treatment of amortization, credits and personnel costs.
